title: Microledger: compact per-model & per-route performance ledger UX
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, high-density "microledger" view for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance signals (latency distribution, throughput, token flow, and cost per-token) in a single, scannable row for each route+model pairing. Target audience: SREs and infra-facing PMs who need to triage regressions quickly but also want quick cost signal. The microledger should live as an alternate compact visualization in the Route Detail and Model Overview surfaces and be embeddable as a small tile in the Overview grid.
acceptance_criteria: Single-row microledger shows: p50/p95/p99 latency values, a 24h sparkline band, throughput (rps), avg tokens per request, and estimated cost delta compared to baseline.
Sparkline encodes both latency band (shaded p50->p95) and token-volume tick marks, with hover tooltip revealing precise percentile values and a small historical table.
Microledger supports three density modes: compact (single-line), comfy (single-row with larger hits), and expanded (mini-chart overlay).
Design tokens and color palette follow console accessibility contrast rules; colorblind-safe palette included.
Interaction spec: click row -> focus route detail; right-click -> time-range quick-filter; inline compare button toggles side-by-side diff with another model version.
Prototype validated in user testing with at least 5 SRE/PM participants and tracked UX feedback captured in review_feedback.
Chart spec mapping documented (fields -> encoding) and handed off to ENG with example JSON payloads.
Performance: visual must render up to 500 rows on a page without blocking critical UI (virtualized list guidance included).
design_notes: Microledger is intentionally different from a full dashboard: it favors density and glancing comprehension over deep drilldowns. Each row is like a ledger entry with 6 micro-encodings.

Primary encodings: textual percentile badges (p50/p95/p99), sparkline with shaded band for latency, throughput numeric + compact bar, token microbar (avg tokens + outlier markers), cost delta microchip (green/red), and a smallServiceFlag for caching/kv-hit ratio.
Visual grammar minimizes color usage: use single hue for latency band, grayscale for background sparkline, and accent color for cost delta and anomaly markers.
Accessibility: ensure badges have text alternatives, sparklines receive aria-labels summarizing key stats, and keyboard focus reveals the overlay panel.
Mobile/fold behavior: default to stacked summary (latency p95 + cost delta) with expand to show full microledger overlay.
Trade-offs discussed: heavy density can hide nuance — include explicit affordance to open full performance canvas for deep inspection.
figma_frames: Frame: Row Overlay — Expanded Mini Chart (ID: LGR-03)
Frame: Comparison Mode — Side-by-side Diff (ID: LGR-04)
review_feedback: PM (Lina Torres): prefer showing p95 as primary headline metric with subtle p50/p99 beside it — p95 is what SLO-focused teams scan for.
Eng (Jinsoo Kim): need explicit guidelines for data sampling and aggregation window; recommend server-side precomputed pcts for 1m/5m/1h buckets to keep rendering fast.
SRE feedback: add KV-cache hit mini-heat indicator because many high-latency spikes correlate with cache misses.
Design review: decrease iconography and rely on micro-typography to reduce visual noise; increase hit target size for keyboard users.
Accessibility reviewer: ensure colorblind palette; provide non-color cues for cost delta (arrow and +/-) and anomaly badges with textual summary.
User test note: participants liked the cost-delta chip but requested clearer baseline definition; add tooltip: 'baseline = route mean last 7d'.
decisions: Primary latency shown: p50 (subtle), p95 (prominent), p99 (compact) — p95 is the primary alerting metric.
Traffic aggregation window default: 1h for sparklines with quick-switch to 5m/24h.
Default sort: by highest p95 regression compared to baseline; user can pin custom sort.
Encoding choices: shaded band for p50->p95, thin line for p99 overlay, vertical micro-ticks for token-volume sampling.
Export: include CSV export of displayed microledger rows and a deep-link to the full Route Performance canvas.
Virtualization guidance: render only visible rows and use server-side lightweight payloads to avoid client jank.
next_steps: Refine Figma frames per review notes and publish updated prototype by 2026-03-05.
Hand off chart-spec mapping and example telemetry JSON to ENG (ENG-2384) with encoding keys and sample values.
Schedule 30-minute design review w/ SREs and PMs to review the final microledger interactions and keyboard flows (owner: Marco).
Define analytics goals for A/B test comparing microledger vs existing compact cards (KPIs: time-to-triage, clicks-to-detail, adoption).
Prepare implementation checklist for console-2026.04 release, including rollout flags and telemetry gating.
